newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico first-half July CPI rose 0.48 percent.
newsitem.headline: Mexico first-half July CPI rose 0.48 percent.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index rose 0.48 percent in the first half of July from the last two weeks of June, Banco de Mexico said on Thursday.
It said that the basic basket of consumer goods rose 0.44 percent in the first two weeks of July from the two weeks before.

Inflation for the first half of July was slightly lower than the 0.49 percent reported in the first half of June and the lowest half-month figure since the peso crisis of December 1994, Banco de Mexico said.

It said that the main causes of inflation in this period were increases in prices of fruits and vegetables, rents, natural gas, bus and air fares, local telephone service, gasoline, electricity, entertainment and other products.
